newsitem.title: UK: Thai, Malaysian airlines opt for Boeing superjumbo.
newsitem.headline: Thai, Malaysian airlines opt for Boeing superjumbo.

text.p: Thai Airways and Malaysia Airlines have signed letters of intent to purchase the planned stretched "superjumbo" version of the Boeing 747 that can carry nearly 600 passengers, the Independent on Sunday said.
The UK paper described the plans as an important breakthrough in the battle between Boeing and Airbus for supremacy in the very large aircraft market, which could be worth up to $200 billion.
"With launch customers now lined up, Boeing will be able to press ahead with developing stretched versions of the 747-400, which it hopes to have in service within four years," the paper said.
The two aircraft manufacturers have been unable to agree on a collaborative approach to a new super jumbo and are therefore offering customers rival versions, it added.

Boeing's designs are further advanced than those of Airbus, which will allow its planes to be in service up to four years earlier, but Airbus argues that customers should wait because its version will be cheaper to run. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
